Consider a logistic regression model trained to detect spam emails. Emails containing harmful phishing links are labeled as spam (1), while regular emails are labeled as not spam (0). A good spam detector should correctly identify almost all emails with phishing links. Even a single phishing email incorrectly classified as not spam could expose users to significant risks. However, the detector may classify some regular emails as spam. This trade-off is acceptable to ensure safety. To ensure user safety, if the threshold is set to a low value to prioritize the detection of phishing emails, type 1. If the threshold is set to a high value to minimize false positives (misclassifying regular emails as spam), type 0.
